import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a more descriptive column for has_video_4k for better legend readability
df['4k_video_support'] = df['has_video_4k'].map({0: 'No 4K Video', 1: 'Has 4K Video'})

# Set a visually appealing style for the plot

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 9)) # Set a larger figure size for better readability
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',      # Color points by sensor type
    style='4k_video_support', # Use different markers for 4K video support
    s=120,                  # Adjust point size for better visibility
    alpha=0.7,              # Add transparency to handle potential overplotting
    palette='viridis'       # Choose a color palette
)

# Add title and labels with improved font sizes
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type and 4K Video Capability', fontsize=18, pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14)

# Improve tick label sizes
plt.xticks(fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

# Place the legend outside the plot area to avoid obscuring data
# The legend will automatically combine hue and style entries.
plt.legend(title='Camera Specifications', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels or legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.88, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend on the right
